overview: Black challenges the centre with ...d5 after 1...Nc6. After 3.e5 Bf5 White gets a French-Advance-like space edge with the bishop outside the chain, and 3.exd5 Qxd5 gives Scandinavian-like play with an early queen and tempo for White's Nf3 or Nc3. White has more space and Black aims for ...e6, ...Nge7, ...f6 and ...Qd7 counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Advance e5, Nf3, Be2 and c3 with a space edge and kingside play
After exd5 Qxd5, Nf3 and Be2 gaining time against the queen

black_ideas.idea: Attack the d4 pawn with ...Bf5, ...e6, ...Qd7 and ...f6 or ...Nge7
Develop the queen early in the Scandinavian lines and rely on solid structure

typical_structures.structure: Advance structure with White e5/d4 against Black e6/d5 and Bf5 outside the chain

character.notes: Black's structure is French-like, hard to crack but cramped; slow play.

soundness.notes: Playable, only Kasparov and Keene doubted it; not refuted.

structure.notes: Advance chain d4/e5 locks the centre; the Exchange variant would be semi-open.

approach.notes: Rare at the top; mostly a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Plans clear after the Advance, but it needs a feel for ...f6 breaks.

sublines_that_differ.name: Exchange
sublines_that_differ.how: Scandinavian structure with an early queen, more open.

character.reason: Black has a sturdy pawn chain in the Advance line, without sharp theory.

structure.reason: The Advance chain locks the centre.

level.reason: Plans are French-like, little forcing theory.

plans.reason: White gains space and Black has to find room.
